analysis_sections.text: The reconstruction preserves recognizable elements of the smiling face while changing the contrast and visibility of features across broad bands. This is useful to compare against the original crop with the same expression. It illustrates a graph-filtered view, rather than a photograph of editing artifacts. The classifier contributions and intervention results provide the separate evidence connecting model features and selected input regions to the prediction.

analysis_sections.text: The middle displayed pair has a positive peak in the upper central grid. Across the displayed pairs, the distribution extends through facial locations that are distinct from the viewer-right boundary selection. These are signed classifier readouts, so their colors describe support for or against the manipulated margin. Their spatial difference from the selected region is informative without establishing a visible editing defect or a failure of either map.

analysis_sections.text: The learned proposal emphasizes the viewer-right crop edge, including hair and the adjacent background margin. The connected region summarizes part of that focus. Attention comes from a separate explanation head operating on frozen detector features, and is unsigned; it does not indicate whether a patch supports the real or fake class in the classifier readout. This explains why it can differ from the contribution view.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: Hiding the selected boundary patches reduces fake support, and restoring them into the reference image recovers it. The saved whole-curve and endpoint comparisons favor the candidate over the displayed strongest controls across the recorded modes and families. With the accompanying source and stability checks, this supports a local model-reliance explanation. The hair/background location should be retained rather than relabeled as a mouth or eye defect.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A blonde woman smiles and speaks in a close interview shot against a dark background with a red side panel. Across the consecutive windows, her lips, gaze and head position change slightly. The original footage supplies a realistic-looking speaking portrait; the explanation views show how the detector responds to that same face and its surrounding crop.

SSTGNN strongly favors manipulated. Signed contribution peaks occur in upper and central facial grid locations, while the selected attention region runs along the viewer-right crop boundary near the hair and background. The recorded regional tests support model reliance on that boundary region, illustrating that different explanation views can emphasize different locations.
inherited_editor_changes.before: The subject appears in a well-lit studio setting with consistent lighting, natural facial expression, and coherent hair strands against a dark backdrop with red side panels. A smooth smile and stable head pose are maintained across sparse original frames and two short consecutive sequences, with no visible warping, texture breaks, or motion artifacts in those windows. The detector delivers an extremely confident fake assessment, driven by spectral and spatial patterns that the explanation head localizes to upper-face regions, while region tests confirm strong model reliance on the viewer-right hair-background boundary despite its visual subtlety.
